behavior: Flies slowly over water while scanning, then plunge-dives for fish. Roosts in flocks, often with other terns and gulls, and nests colonially or in solitary pairs near water.
field_marks: Very large, heavy-bodied tern with a large head and thick neck
Massive, straight coral-red bill, often with a dusky tip
Black cap and short crest; forehead becomes white-flecked outside breeding plumage
White body with a pale gray back and upperwings
Dark eyes and short blackish legs and feet
Broad, pointed wings with dark outer primaries below; short, shallowly forked tail
habitat: Freshwater and saltwater shorelines, including large lakes, rivers, estuaries, lagoons, beaches, and islands. Nests on flat, open, sparsely vegetated sand, gravel, mud, or shell-covered ground.
